questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Merge sort always has more number of swap than comparison.
S2 : Prim’s algorithm always makes a tree in any step for finding MST.
The number of correct statements is/are

NAT
questions.solution:
(1)
• Merge Sort doesn’t perform swaps; it only compares and merges elements. So, it doesn’t have more swaps than comparisons. So, S1 is Incorrect.
• Prim’s algorithm builds a tree at every step while finding the Minimum Spanning Tree. So, S2 is correct.

questions.solution:
(a)
• Ο(V): Time taken to build the vertices min heap.
• Ο(V log V): Extract minimum vertex and heapify.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : For every weighted graph with starting vertex at S, Bellman Ford algorithm always gives shortest path to any given vertex V.
S2 : If a graph contain a negative weight cycle then Dijkstra’s algorithm may not terminate.
Which of the above is incorrect?
questions.solution:
(a)
S1 : Bellman Ford algorithm may not give shortest path if it contain negative weight cycle. So, S1 is incorrect.
S2 : Dijkstra’s algorithm may give incorrect result if it contain negative weight cycle but it always terminate.
So, S2 is incorrect.
